rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 (b0883c17) was REVISE on a gating HIGH from editquality, and the objection was RIGHT and is the most valuable thing in this round: `modalTag` broke ties with `tag > best` — a LEXICAL comparison, in the same file as, and one screen below, the numeric comparator written to fix exactly that. A tie between five workloads on v1.0.999 and five on v1.0.1000 picks v1.0.999 as the fleet tag (lexically higher, numerically older), and because the fleet tag is the single value every straggler and ahead-of-fleet finding is measured against, that inverts the ENTIRE report rather than one line of it. Note what this makes it: the SAME defect three times in one file — once in the shipped report (the live run that called two hand-deployed services 'old'), once in the first repair for it, and once here in the tie-break. The lesson, written at the function: A HELPER THAT DOES THE COMPARISON CORRECTLY DOES NOT PROTECT THE CALL SITES THAT DO NOT USE IT. Fixed to call compareTags, with a deterministic lexical fall-back only for tags that cannot be ordered at all, and MUTATION-PROVEN the decisive way round: restoring `tag > best` makes the new test fail with its own message.

ORIGINAL RATIONALE FOLLOWS. bugs_open/318, phase 2 — the CLUSTER half. The gate shipped this morning (register BLD-026, council-approved 83442a5a) reads the FILESYSTEM and asks 'can a release reach this service?'. It is preventive and it refuses. It is also, by construction, blind to two shapes, and BOTH were found by hand while measuring on 2026-08-22: `capped-schedule-ordering-check` had an overlay, a dockerfile, build/push/deploy targets and membership of both release lists, and NO CronJob in the cluster at all (declared everywhere, running nowhere); and `site-discovery-staleness-check` / `site-locale-unset-check` were running as CronJobs with no `overlays/` tree on disk (running with nothing on disk describing them). Neither is visible to a filesystem gate, in either direction, ever, because THE FILESYSTEM AND THE CLUSTER ARE TWO ENUMERATIONS AND NEITHER IS A SUPERSET OF THE OTHER. This adds the cluster-side comparison as three predicates plus a `--census` mode. It DETECTS rather than prevents, and that is a stated limit rather than a stage on the way to something better: a cluster-side absence has no commit to gate. THE FIRST LIVE RUN FOUND A DEFECT IN ITS OWN REPORT, which is the most useful thing in this submission: it called two services on v1.0.1324 'RUNNING AN OLD FLEET TAG' against a fleet on v1.0.1323. They were NEWER, hand-deployed. A report that states the opposite of the truth is worse than one that stays quiet — a reader chasing a frozen service finds one that is, if anything, too new, and concludes the instrument works. Fixed by splitting the finding by DIRECTION, with numeric rather than lexical tag ordering (this estate is on v1.0.13xx, so it has already crossed v1.0.999 -> v1.0.1000 where a string comparison says 999 is newer) and an explicit third answer for tags that cannot be ordered at all. SCOPE, stated so it is not over-read: this is HAND-RUN ONLY. No CronJob, no RBAC manifest, no doc_notes row. Scheduling it is a separate decision with its own round, and the split is deliberate — this estate's own measured lesson is 'detection works; SCHEDULE and DISPATCH do not', so a detector and its driver should not be claimed together.

edits.rationale: ROUND 2 CHANGE — the gating fix. modalTag now breaks ties with compareTags instead of `>` on strings. Everything else in this edit is unchanged. The predicates take a []Workload, NOT a Kubernetes client, so the whole census is table-testable with no cluster — a predicate that could only be exercised against a live cluster is a predicate nobody exercises. Three refusals are load-bearing and each has a test: (1) an empty read is an ERROR, not a clean result, because zero of our workloads means the wrong namespace, lost RBAC or a dead fleet, and none of those is 'nothing is wrong'; (2) a fleet with no readable tag is an error, not a silent pass; (3) an unorderable tag gets its own finding kind rather than a guessed direction. Staleness is measured against the MODAL tag rather than the makefile's IMAGE_TAG, because IMAGE_TAG is what the NEXT release will use — between a bump and the release every service would read as stale against it. Ties break toward the lexically higher tag so a fleet mid-rollout measures against what it is moving TO, else every release day produces a page of findings about services that are about to be fine.

edits.rationale: ROUND 2 CHANGE — adds TestModalTag_TieBreaksNumericallyNotLexically, which the second objection asked for: the 999/1000 boundary was pinned for compareTags and NOT for the fleet-tag selection path, so the gating bug would have shipped green. It asserts four things: the tie picks v1.0.1000; the end-to-end census on that fleet reports the 999 pair as BEHIND and never the 1000 pair as AHEAD; a clear 3-2 majority still wins outright so the tie-break does not become the rule; and an unorderable tie is DETERMINISTIC across 20 calls, because a report that changes run to run is not reproducible. Mutation-proven the decisive way round: restoring `tag > best` fails it with its own message. A detector's clean first run on a healthy fleet could only have come out clean, so the discriminating power lives here. The negative control is FIRST on purpose — noise is fatal to a report, and a census that fires on a coherent fleet stops being read. The ahead-of-fleet case pins the defect the live run exposed and would fail if the false 'OLD' wording came back. TestCompareTags pins the v1.0.999 -> v1.0.1000 boundary, which is not theoretical: this estate is on v1.0.13xx, so a lexical comparison would silently invert every finding across it. The rollout case pins that a fleet mid-release measures against the tag it is moving TO. The empty-read case is the demand control — wrong namespace, lost RBAC and a dead fleet all produce zero findings, and zero findings is what healthy looks like.

ROUND 2 — the reuse objection is ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE, and its premise turns out to be wrong. The seat's claim was that the named CronJob check services 'must already list/read cluster workloads to do their jobs'. They do not: they read POSTGRES. `shared-output-fields-check` runs `./config-key-audit --shared-output-fields --report`, and that binary's own dockerfile header states it reads 'DIRECTLY from Postgres (PG_CLIENTS_HOST in the CronJob env; NO KUBECTL IN THIS IMAGE, no pods/exec RBAC — see cmd/config-key-audit/fleetdb.go)'. `component-render-check` and `verifier-remit-check` run their own binaries against the DB; `optional-key-budget-check` and `site-discovery-staleness-check` run `postgres:16-alpine` with an inline script and carry no binary of ours at all. THE THREE MEASUREMENTS: (1) `grep -rln 'kubernetes.NewForConfig' --include=*.go .` returns SIX call sites and not one shared wrapper — spawn_actions.go, diagnose_build_gate_action.go, agent_image.go, thunder/ssh/secrets.go, cmd/remote-job-spawner/main.go, and this file; each bootstraps inline, and agent_image.go is `rest.InClusterConfig()` ONLY with no kubeconfig path, so it cannot serve a hand-run CLI. (2) `grep -rn 'Deployments(.*).List(|CronJobs(.*).List(|DaemonSets(.*).List('` over every .go file returns ZERO hits outside this file — nothing in the estate has ever listed a workload. (3) No check service's CMD reaches the API. So there was nothing to reuse. WHAT THE OBJECTION DID SURFACE, recorded rather than acted on: six inline NewForConfig sites IS a real extraction opportunity, and it is deliberately NOT taken here — touching five unrelated call sites inside a bug-fix round is the scope shape the guardian seat vetoes, and rightly. Named as a follow-up in the lane docs so its absence reads as a decision. On the seat's second point: `check-release-coverage` has no cluster-reading arm and never had one; this is not a parallel tool but the SAME binary and the same Decl parse, which is exactly why it is a flag rather than a second command — a second binary would be a second place for the declaration reader to drift. The only part that talks to Kubernetes, kept OUT of pkg/releaseset so the package never imports client-go and the predicates stay testable without a cluster. It lists Deployments, CronJobs AND DaemonSets: all three carry one of our images today, and reading only Deployments would have missed every frozen check service, which is most of this bug's evidence. A LIST ERROR IS RETURNED, NEVER SWALLOWED — if the CronJob list fails and the Deployment list succeeds, silently returning the Deployments would report a clean fleet while blind to every scheduled check, which is the exact population this bug is about. A partial read is not a read. Both auth paths are first-class rather than one being a fallback: in-cluster is how a future CronJob would run it, kubeconfig is how it is run by hand today, and rest.InClusterConfig fails fast and unambiguously when the service-account files are absent so it can never half-succeed against the wrong cluster. Read-only: it lists, and does nothing else.

Two modes on one binary, and the header now states plainly that they ask DIFFERENT questions so one is never read as the other: the default reads the filesystem and REFUSES, --census reads the cluster and only REPORTS. Same binary because they share the makefile parse and the same Decl, and a second binary would be a second place for the declaration reader to drift — the 099 roster-mirror class.

The rider, named rather than hidden. A `release-census` target, because a tool nobody can find is a tool nobody runs — this estate's own lesson about detectors with no reader. Its comment states the split between the two modes and, explicitly, that this is HAND-RUN ONLY: no CronJob, no RBAC, no doc_notes row, so it must not be described as a live detector. That scoping is deliberate rather than unfinished — 'detection works; SCHEDULE and DISPATCH do not' is a measured finding on this estate, so a detector and its driver are not claimed together.

grounded_in: [MEASURED 2026-08-22, first live run] `make release-census` against ai-persona-system: '29 of 45 workloads run a docker.io/aqls/ image; the fleet is on v1.0.1323', 5 findings, ZERO false positives. Two AHEAD OF THE FLEET (commit-sha-exposure-check, content-loss-check on v1.0.1324, both hand-deployed), one BEHIND (optional-explicit-wires-check on v1.0.1321), two DECLARED BUT NOT RUNNING (capped-schedule-ordering-check, component-source-vocabulary-check). Every one corresponds to something separately verified by hand or stated in another lane's own commit message ('NOT yet built or deployed').

[MEASURED 2026-08-22] The defect this round's own first live run exposed: before the direction split, the two v1.0.1324 services were reported as 'RUNNING AN OLD FLEET TAG' against a fleet on v1.0.1323. They were newer. Fixed by splitting the kind by direction and ordering tags numerically.
bugs_open/318, 'How to verify a fix': 'The instrument must be shown able to fail... a compliant tree must stay green. A green gate on a compliant tree proves nothing — it could only have passed.'

register BLD-022, 'what it deliberately does NOT catch' (i): 'a service in the list with no overlay at $(OVERLAY_PATH) — deploy-agents warns and skips'. The cluster-side twin of that gap is what declaredNotRunning covers, and it was never in the gate's reach.

bugs_open/237 handoff, Decision B: 'each overlay was written once, on the day the service was created, and never again... The failure is silent by construction: a service with its own deploy target and no caller emits nothing, and the natural check ("is the image live?") reads healthy because it looks at the pod, which is running perfectly — just old.' That sentence is the straggler predicate's whole justification.

MEMORY / estate lesson: 'detection works; SCHEDULE and DISPATCH do not' — the reason this round ships the detector hand-run and leaves the CronJob, its RBAC and its doc_notes row to a separate decision rather than claiming them together.
LANDMINES.md: 'a same-tag rebuild ships the node's stale cached binary' — the reason an AHEAD OF THE FLEET finding's remedy is 'the next release MUST NOT reuse this tag' rather than 'roll it back'.
plan.risks: ROUND 2 NOTE: the round-1 gating defect (modalTag's lexical tie-break) is FIXED and mutation-proven; the reuse objection is answered with three measurements rather than a change, and the follow-up it surfaced (six inline k8s client bootstraps, no shared wrapper) is named as deliberately out of scope for a bug-fix round. FOUR, named. (1) A DETECTOR WITH NO DRIVER IS THIS ESTATE'S DOCUMENTED FAILURE MODE. Stated rather than mitigated: this round ships hand-run only, the makefile comment says so in capitals, and scheduling is a separate decision. The alternative — claiming the CronJob in the same round — is what 'detection works; schedule and dispatch do not' was written about. (2) NOISE. A report that fires on a coherent fleet stops being read, and this estate has measured that decay (an agreed invariant with no teeth was violated by 84% of the anchors it governed). Mitigated by the negative control being the FIRST test, by the modal-tag choice (IMAGE_TAG would flag everything between a bump and a release), by the rollout tie-break, and by treating all three declaring lists as 'declared' so a reviewed OWN_LINEAGE exemption is never nagged about. Live evidence: 5 findings on 45 workloads, all true. (3) TAG ORDERING IS A HEURISTIC. compareTags handles vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and REFUSES anything else with its own finding kind rather than guessing; the v1.0.999 -> v1.0.1000 boundary is pinned by a test because this estate has already crossed it. A tag scheme change would produce 'cannot be ordered' findings — loud and correct, not silent. (4) FIRST-CONTAINER-ONLY. readWorkloads reads container[0] of each workload; a sidecar carrying one of our images would be missed. Accepted because no workload on this estate has one today, and stated so the absence reads as a decision — but note this is the same shape as the images-block cap the council caught in round 1, so if a sidecar ever appears this is where to look. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: no CronJob/RBAC/doc_notes (above); no auto-remediation (the census reports, acting is human or work-item territory); no comparison of an image's CONTENTS to its tag (that is BLD-019/BLD-020's territory and duplicating it here would give two answers to one question); no staleness-vs-source check (OWNER RULED OUT 2026-08-22, 'we can skip the 18 August staleness build' — recorded so its absence is not re-filed as a gap).
